name: Islam
subtitle: Submission to the one God, in the tradition of the prophets

adherents.basis: Enumerated by Pew. 25.6% of world population. Supersedes the v5 stat box figure of 1.9 bn.

overview.body: Islam holds that God is one, without partner, likeness, or need, and that the [[quran|Quran]] is God's final revelation, delivered through Muhammad, the seal of a line of prophets that includes Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus. The word islam means submission: the fitting response of the creature to the Creator, and the religion's name for itself describes an act rather than a founder. A Muslim's life is structured by five obligatory practices, from the profession of faith to the pilgrimage at Mecca, and by a moral law understood to cover all of life. From one city in seventh-century Arabia, Islam grew within a century into a civilization reaching from the Atlantic to the Indus; today its two billion adherents make it the world's second-largest religion and its fastest-growing, with its demographic heart in South and Southeast Asia rather than the Arab lands of its birth.

origins.body: According to Islamic tradition, revelation began in 610 CE when Muhammad, a forty-year-old merchant of Mecca in retreat on Mount Hira, was commanded by the angel Gabriel to recite. The revelations continued for twenty-three years, and their gathered text is the Quran. Mecca's ruling clans met the message of one God and a coming judgment with escalating hostility, and in 622 the small community migrated north to Yathrib, thereafter Medina: the [[hijra|Hijra]], from which the Islamic calendar counts. In Medina the community became a polity, and the decade that followed brought the battles, treaties, and conversions through which Mecca itself entered Islam without a sack in 630. By Muhammad's death in 632 most of Arabia had joined the new order, and the question his death left open, who rightly leads the community, became in time the deepest division within it: those who held that leadership passed to the community's chosen caliphs became the Sunni majority, and those who held that it belonged to the Prophet's house through Ali became the Shia.

core_beliefs.body: At the center is [[tawhid]], the absolute oneness of God: the sin Islam calls unforgivable if unrepented is shirk, associating partners with God, and the tradition's art, law, and mysticism are all shaped by that refusal. Faith is classically summarized in six articles: God; the angels; the revealed books, of which the Quran is the final and protected form; the prophets, culminating in Muhammad; the Day of Judgment, when every soul is weighed; and the divine decree, God's encompassing knowledge and will. The human being is not fallen but forgetful, and revelation is a reminder; each person is born capable of submission and answerable for their own deeds, with no intermediary between the worshipper and God. Paradise and fire are described with concrete vividness according to the Quran, and God's mercy is repeatedly declared to outrun his wrath.

canon.title: The hadith collections
canon.status: Sunni Islam holds six collections canonical, with Bukhari and Muslim preeminent; Shia Islam relies on its own Four Books; status differs by branch and school

practices.name: Shahada
practices.summary: The profession of faith: there is no god but God, and Muhammad is the messenger of God. Saying it with intent is how one enters Islam.

practices.name: Salat
practices.summary: The five daily prayers facing Mecca, from dawn to night, in prescribed words and movements; Friday's midday prayer is congregational.

practices.name: Zakat
practices.summary: The obligatory alms, classically a fortieth of qualifying wealth each year, owed to the poor and other named categories.

practices.name: Sawm
practices.summary: The dawn-to-dusk fast of [[ramadan]], abstaining from food, drink, and marital relations, commemorating the Quran's first descent.

practices.name: Hajj
practices.frequency: Once in a lifetime, for those able
practices.summary: The pilgrimage to Mecca in the sacred month, obligatory once for every Muslim able to perform it, ending in the feast of sacrifice.

rites.name: Birth
rites.summary: The call to prayer is whispered into the newborn's ear; on the seventh day many families name the child and offer the aqiqah sacrifice.

rites.name: Circumcision
rites.summary: Male circumcision is near-universal practice, its timing varying by region and school.

rites.name: Marriage
rites.summary: The nikah is a contract before witnesses with an agreed gift to the bride; it is a solemn covenant but not a sacrament.

rites.name: Funeral
rites.summary: The dead are washed, shrouded, prayed over in the janazah prayer, and buried facing Mecca, ideally before the day ends; mourning is restrained and cremation is prohibited.

misconceptions.correction: In Islamic teaching, worship is directed to God alone. Muhammad is revered as the final prophet and moral exemplar, and is not held to be divine; venerating him as such would contradict tawhid itself.

The word means striving. It covers the moral struggle of the self and, in law, regulated armed conflict with strict limits; equating it with indiscriminate war is rejected by mainstream scholarship in every school.

misconceptions.claim: Muslims are Arabs and Islam is an Arab religion.
misconceptions.correction: Arabs are roughly a fifth of Muslims. The largest Muslim populations are in Indonesia, Pakistan, India, and Bangladesh, and Islam's demographic center is South and Southeast Asia.

Islam contains branches, law schools, theological traditions, and currents, Sunni, Shia, and Ibadi, four Sunni law schools, Sufi orders, and modern movements, that differ as consequentially as the branches of any world religion.
